hints.title: Minimise in x first
hints.body: For a fixed k, the term 2(x−k2)2 is nonnegative and vanishes at x=k2. Read the remaining vertex height.
hints.recap: In completed-square form, the square fixes the minimizing input and the constant fixes the height.
hints.pitfall: Do not minimise k before identifying each curve’s lowest point.
hints.pause: Write the vertex coordinates in terms of k.

recall.reminder: In completed-square form, the square fixes the minimizing input and the constant fixes the height.

hints.title: Compare the vertex heights
hints.body: The lowest height for a given k is k22+4k+3. Complete this square in k.
hints.recap: After finding one curve’s minimum, optimise its height across the parameter family.
hints.pitfall: The factor <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> must apply to the entire completed square.
hints.pause: Complete the square in the parameter to expose the smallest possible vertex height.

hints.title: Recover both coordinates
hints.body: Find the parameter that makes the completed square in the vertex height vanish. Use that same parameter in the original vertex-coordinate expression to obtain the horizontal coordinate.
hints.recap: Use one consistent parameter value to attain the overall bound.
hints.pitfall: The requested <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> includes the input coordinate as well as the minimum height.
hints.pause: Complete the parameter minimisation, recover both coordinates of the attaining point and add them.

recall.reminder: In completed-square form, attain the minimum by making the square zero and recover the corresponding input.

solution:
For fixed k, the curve is yk=2(x−k2)2+k22+4k+3. Its minimum occurs at x=k2 and has height k22+4k+3.

Complete the second square: k22+4k+3=12(k+4)2−5≥−5. Equality is attained at k=−4. For that curve the minimizing x is k2=−2, so the overall lowest point is (a, b)=(−2, −5).

Therefore a+b=−7, option D. Both square terms vanish at the stated pair, proving the lower bound is attained.
knowledgePattern: Minimise vertex height across a parameterised quadratic family
